A Buddhist temple on the slopes of Mount Toham near Gyeongju, South Korea, rebuilt on a grand scale from 751 under Unified Silla. Its name means temple of the Buddha land.

The minister Kim Daeseong began the work, and the state finished it in 774. Much of the wooden temple burned during the Imjin War of the 1590s, but the stone parts are original:

  • The Dabotap and Seokgatap pagodas, a pair of contrasting stone towers.
  • The stone stairways and bridges that lead up to the main halls.
  • Two gilt bronze Buddha statues.

Higher on the mountain lies the Seokguram grotto, built at the same time: an artificial domed cave holding a great granite Buddha, often called the finest work of Korean Buddhist sculpture. Inside the Seokgatap pagoda, a printed charm found in 1966 may be one of the oldest surviving woodblock prints. Bulguksa and Seokguram became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995.
sum: A Buddhist temple on the slopes of Mount Toham near Gyeongju, South Korea, rebuilt on a grand scale from 751 under Unified Silla. Its name means temple of the Buddha land.
